mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (t-test p>0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 8.5%, it signals a weak labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when UNRATE > 8.5% (t-test p>0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A rising inflation rate (CPIAUCSL > 0.3% MoM) combined with stagnant monetary policy (FEDFUNDS unchanged for 3 months) signals an emerging inflationary threat that triggers equity sell-offs, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 0.3% MoM and FEDFUNDS unchanged for 3 months
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window, or negative returns do not occur in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply shock regime characterized by declining industrial production (INDPRO < 95.0), manufacturing output contraction reduces corporate profits and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0 (t-test p>0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS growth > 0.2% MoM) signals improving labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS growth > 0.2% MoM (t-test p>0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 550,000 units, it signals a weakening residential sector that reduces consumer confidence and corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when HOUST < 550.0 (t-test p>0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY), persistent price pressures force the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY (t-test p>0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE > 8.5%) combined with weak housing starts (HOUST < 600.0) signals a dual stress in labor and housing markets that depresses consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window, or negative returns do not occur in > 60% of triggered instances.
